The current government's term has less than a year remaining. After lawmakers returned from Beijing on a "study and exchange" programme, Chief Executive John Lee held the first "dialogue and exchange session" today (the 28th). The closed-door meeting took place in the Legislative Council banquet hall and lasted about 1.5 hours. The Chief Executive and Legislative Council President Starry Lee met the media afterwards. Lee said he had engaged in "warm and in-depth" exchanges with 67 lawmakers without any restrictions, strengthening consensus like "members of Team Hong Kong." Lee Wai-kuk also said the executive and legislature are "in the same boat," and that the Legislative Council, as the government's partner in governing Hong Kong and driving reform, means "we are all members of Team Hong Kong."

Chief Executive John Lee and Legislative Council President Starry Lee meet the media after the dialogue and exchange session.

After the dialogue and exchange session, Chief Executive John Lee and Legislative Council President Starry Lee met reporters. Lee said he had warm and in-depth exchanges with the 67 lawmakers, enhancing mutual understanding, narrowing the distance between them, and sharing his thoughts on "patriots governing Hong Kong." He described the legislature as the government's reform partner, noting that the executive and legislature share the same goal of solving problems for the public. Through dialogue and exchange, they can connect different perspectives, see things from each other's point of view, and strike a balance between checks and cooperation. This helps foster consensus between the executive and legislature, allowing them to focus more on getting things done.

Lee added that under executive-led governance, he constantly considers how to keep creating new value for "patriots governing Hong Kong." This dialogue session is one such innovative initiative. In a relaxed setting with no procedural rules, "the Chief Executive and lawmakers chatted like members of Team Hong Kong," with no restrictions, allowing warm and in-depth discussions of issues. The exchange was not limited to one-on-one conversations; multiple lawmakers could engage in in-depth discussions on the same topic simultaneously, sharing their thoughts and feelings, adding a human touch to communication.

John Lee says he held warm and in-depth discussions with lawmakers in the absence of any procedural rules.

Lee also spoke at length about his thoughts on "patriots governing Hong Kong," noting that the reform process will affect many entrenched interests, making solutions hard to find. He said the executive and legislature must handle systemic relationships — micro versus macro, comprehensive versus partial, immediate versus long-term, special versus general, and primary versus secondary — in order to achieve a high degree of consensus and deliver results. He described today's exchange as positive and constructive, saying the experience would be reviewed for room for improvement. He also said he had listened to lawmakers' accounts of their Beijing study trip and found the national policies and their implementation worthy of reference.

Starry Lee said the exchange session was very successful, with one outcome being that lawmakers, having drawn inspiration from Beijing's 12345 hotline, proposed a visit to study 1823, which the Chief Executive has noted and agreed to.

Starry Lee: Very successful, nothing off-limits

Starry Lee described the exchange session as very successful, saying 15 lawmakers had shared their views and spoken, including sharing the insights from their Beijing study and exchange trip last week, making it "a truly wide-ranging discussion." She said the executive and legislature are "in the same boat," with the Legislative Council serving as the government's partner in governing Hong Kong and pushing reform, meaning "we are all members of Team Hong Kong." She expressed confidence that as long as the executive and legislature continue to maintain positive interaction and efficient collaboration through different channels, stay people-centred, and learn from the country's successful experience, they will be better placed to resolve issues for the public.

She also noted that the 15 lawmakers who spoke shared the "outcomes of their Beijing study." Several lawmakers had earlier visited Beijing's 12345 Citizen Hotline Service Centre. She cited as an example a lawmaker's suggestion of visiting Hong Kong's 1823 to learn how to better serve the public, and said the Chief Executive had noted and agreed to lawmakers visiting 1823.

The current government has introduced multiple measures said to improve executive-legislature relations, including setting up "frontbench exchange sessions" for officials and lawmakers to communicate on policies, and changing the Chief Executive's Question and Answer sessions into "interactive exchange Q&A sessions." In a recent letter to the Legislative Council, the Administration Wing said the dialogue and exchange session was designed to allow everyone to "engage in warm and in-depth direct exchanges" in a relaxed setting. The Chief Executive would first share his practical thoughts on "patriots governing Hong Kong," after which an open dialogue would follow with no restrictions on topics, which could cover national, Hong Kong and international affairs, with flexible content.
